question.problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.000\,3$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
125,\,50,\,20,\,8,\,…
$$
question.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=125$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{50}{125}=\frac{2}{5}.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =125{(\frac{2}{5})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $0.000\,3.$
Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & <0.000\,3 \\ 125{(\frac{2}{5})}^{n-1} & <0.000\,3 \\ {(\frac{2}{5})}^{n-1} & <\frac{0.000\,3}{125} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡{(\frac{2}{5})}^{n-1} & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,002\,4) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{2}{5}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,002\,4) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,002\,4)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{2}{5})} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,002\,4)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{2}{5})}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we reversed the inequality sign when divided by $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{2}{5})$ because $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{2}{5})$ is a negative number. 

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,002\,4)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{2}{5})}+1≈15.122
$$

Therefore, the $16$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $0.000\,3.$
